Quistchurch, West Central, Wayne and Elections coming up on the 19th.

Train nurse,
train drug consular, former Electract University West Indies KFL Campus,
former tutor at the Bible Discommunic College,
author, writer and now I'm finishing off law at University West Indies KFL Campus.
So what's your area of focus going into?
I'm trying to farm a guy.
We're focusing on many aspects.
The manifesto will be launched tomorrow,
and that will give you a detailed focus of what the Democratic Labour Party
is supposed to do.
But I can say a little bit about what I intend to do
for my constituents in Quistchurch Central, West Central.
Could you outline some of the areas?
Absolutely.
First, we want to build a state of the art sport in complex at Canville in the area.
And this is not only for persons to play sports,
but this facility will be available for persons to look for spectators to take part.
We're looking at a wealth creation program,
and I think that that's important to persons in my constituency.
I want to be able to encourage persons to build wealth in Barbados,
and I think that that's critical to the existence of the quality of life
for the individuals in my constituency.
We have a Sikh program, and the acronym Sikh stands for Search,
Employment, Education, and Knowledge.
And I'll spin off from that program.
We'll be looking at offering a mentorship program,
and I believe that mentorship is very important and is critical
in the context of shaping individuals and so on.
And rather than placing persons out there in the dormant to seek a job
and leave them high-end, that is not going to be all focused
and hence the mentorship program is going to be attached to that
to offer support, guidance, information, and so on.
Then we're going to have capacity building program.
And that's important again.
It's going to be designed to shed the lives of the constituents in my area.
We have an anti-drug program.
That's critical, anti-crime program.
We need to keep this constituency safe, and we need to do so,
because many children live in the constituency,
and therefore a safe environment is always best for individuals.
I'm sure this would be coming from based on what you're hearing from a constituency.
And could you say what are some of the sticking points that there are no, you know, discuss it?
Absolutely. One is unemployment. That's a major concern.
And therefore, that's why the search program is going to help buttress that.
And we know that in the context of COVID, many persons have been unemployed.
And therefore employment is the major issue in terms of going far in terms of helping constituents and so on.
How did you get involved in politics?
Well, first of all, I have been engaging in humanitarian work across Barbados for some time now, for a couple of years now.
Throughout COVID, I mean we're still in COVID, but at the beginning of COVID,
and over the past two years, I've been supplying breakfast to healthcare workers
and all the healthcare institutions around Barbados, posted it online,
and Comrade Stephen Blackett saw it and encouraged me to get involved in politics
and thought that I would have been a good person.
First of all, I have the education there. And second of all, it was already helping persons.
As a trainer, I have a background with regards to caring for individuals.
And I believe that it also stemmed from that. I like to help people.
And I like to see them strive in an environment.
And I like to encourage them to strive for better quality life.
And I think that with my help, I can encourage and aspire individuals to do the same.

youtube_description:
Newcomer to the political arena Rennette Dimmott says she is prepared to pull out all the stops to claim victory in the January 19 general elections.

Dimmott, who is gunning for the Christ Church West Central constituency, will be going up against the Barbados Labour Party’s Adrian “Medic” Forde, Solutions Barbados’ Kenneth Lewis and Belfield Belgrave of the Alliance Party for Progress (APP).
